summary: Tested the new Inbound STO Receipt feature end-to-end. Backend: 13/13 pytest cases pass (auth gating 401, /sites, /pending shape + site filter, job-status 404, receive 400/422, already_received short-circuit, post-receive list filtering). Frontend: the reported BLANK PAGE is NOT a rendering bug - the real route is /inventory/inbound-receipts (App.js:119); the main agent tested /inbound-receipts, and App.js has NO catch-all route so any unknown path renders only the Footer. Page itself renders fine with 0 console errors. Found and root-caused a CRITICAL blocker: the Playwright browser binary is unreachable from the supervisor-managed backend process (no PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH), so EVERY receive job failed instantly. After applying a test-env symlink I re-ran the full flow: 2 real SAP Goods Receipts were genuinely posted live (STO-000045/P8D1-182, STO-000035/P8D1-180) with correct progress-step polling, non-closable dialog, success toast, dialog close, list refresh and DB persistence. Separately found that the editable Received Qty feature is completely non-functional (SAP rejects the quantity PATCH as read-only) and the failure is silently swallowed.

critical.issue: Job fails immediately: 'BrowserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at /root/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1234/chrome-linux/headless_shell'. ROOT CAUSE: the chromium build exists at /pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1234 and interactive shells export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/pw-browsers, but the supervisor backend process (/etc/supervisor/conf.d, uvicorn) has NO PLAYWRIGHT_* env vars, so playwright falls back to the default (non-existent) cache dir. This is why the main agent's direct script runs worked but every HTTP-triggered job failed. I applied a TEST-ONLY workaround (symlink /root/.cache/ms-playwright -> /pw-browsers) to unblock testing - needs a real fix (add PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH to backend/.env + restart backend, AND ensure `python -m playwright install chromium` runs in the deployment image, otherwise this feature is 100% broken in production).

The 'editable Received Qty per line' feature does not work at all. inbound_receipt_service.apply_quantity_overrides -> sap_inbound_delivery_client.update_item_quantity PATCH on InboundDeliveryItemQuantityCollection returns HTTP 500 {"code":"ERROR","message":"Changing data not possible; data is read-only"}. Verified twice live: on an already-posted delivery (STO-000032/P8D1-179) AND on a genuinely fresh un-posted one (STO-000035/P8D1-180). The exception is caught and logged only as a WARNING, so the job continues and the Playwright PGR posts the FULL shipped quantity, then the UI toasts '<STO> received in full'. Real impact: user entered 1 EA against 2 EA shipped, SAP received 2 EA, DB recorded receipt_status='received', and the user was told it succeeded in full. Data-integrity + silently-wrong-outcome bug. Fix: set the quantity inside the Playwright PGR screen (it already clicks Propose Quantities) OR fail the job loudly / disable qty editing until supported.

minor.issue: Does the SAP outbound-delivery-id backfill synchronously inside the request; first load took 40s+ (and up to ~5 min while the SAP tenant was intermittently connect-timing-out). No pagination beyond .limit(200) and no per-order timeout - a slow SAP makes the whole page hang on a single request.

job_store.get_job / create_job / update_job are blocking pymongo calls invoked directly on the event loop (neighbouring calls in the same handler correctly use asyncio.to_thread). Minor event-loop blocking under polling load.
No in-progress lock on the STO: two users (or a double-click after a page reload) can start two concurrent Playwright jobs for the same STO/delivery, racing duplicate Goods Receipt posts in live SAP.

Route is `anyUser` and neither the pending list nor the receive action is filtered/validated against the caller's bound_sites - any logged-in user can receive any site's STO. Confirm this is intended (the site dropdown is a UI-only filter).

ui_bugs.issue: No catch-all `<Route path="*">`. Any unknown path (including /inbound-receipts, which the main agent tested) renders a completely blank page with only the footer 'Build c78a544 · 28 Aug 2026' - exactly the reported symptom. The real page at /inventory/inbound-receipts renders correctly with 0 console errors, and the NavTabs link (data-testid=nav-inventory-inbound-receipts) is present and works. Add a 404/redirect route.

When the job returns status='failed', pollReceiveJob throws new Error(job.error) but the catch block only reads e?.response?.data?.detail, so job.error is ALWAYS discarded and the user only ever sees the generic 'Could not post the Goods Receipt.' toast. Observed live: real error was the Playwright launch failure, completely invisible to the user. Also on this path setReceiveTarget(null)/loadOrders() are skipped, so the dialog stays open with no inline error and the row is not refreshed.

Wrapper uses `overflow-hidden` while the table needs 792px. At 768px (clientWidth 718) and 390px (clientWidth 356) the STO column and the Action/Receive button are clipped with NO horizontal scroll (documentElement.scrollWidth == innerWidth, overflow-x: computed 'hidden'), so a real tablet/phone user cannot reach the Receive button. Use overflow-x-auto (or a card layout on small screens).

Raw SAP JSON is shown verbatim to end users, e.g. `P8D1-192: HTTP 500: {"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":{"lang":"en","value":"Action InboundDeliveryRelease not possible; action is disabled"...`. Needs a humanised message (raw text can stay in a tooltip).

Only a min guard exists (confirm correctly disables at 0 and -3), but there is no max: 999 against a shipped qty of 1 keeps Confirm Receipt enabled. Combined with the broken override PATCH, an over-receipt entry is accepted and silently ignored.

'<STO> received in full — closed in SAP.' fires whenever result.status === 'received', even when the user deliberately reduced a line quantity (verified on STO-000032: entered 2 of 3 EA, toast still said 'received in full').
Pre-existing: /inventory shows a bare 'Access Denied' card with no header/NavTabs, so a user granted only Inbound STO Receipt who lands there has no way to navigate back.

integration_issues.flow: Confirm Receipt -> job start -> poll -> toast
integration_issues.issue: VERIFIED WORKING (after the Playwright env fix): POST returns {job_id} immediately (non-blocking), frontend polls /receive-status every ~2.5s (30 polls, all HTTP 200), progress-step text advances 'Starting...' -> 'Logging into SAP...' -> 'Posting Goods Receipt for P8D1-182 (1/1)...' -> 'Done', dialog closes, success toast shown, list refreshes and the received STO disappears. Dialog correctly NON-closable while submitting (ESC ignored, outside-click ignored, Cancel + Confirm + qty inputs all disabled). already_received short-circuit returns {already_received:true,result} with no new job. DB persisted receipt_status='received', receipt_results, received_at, received_by.
BROKEN - the edited quantity never reaches SAP (see backend critical #2); the job reports success anyway.

issues: Looks good: teal header, readable contrast, clear status pills, expandable line-item detail, delivery-notification ids surfaced. No console errors.
receipt_error text is truncated with `truncate` but the title tooltip carries the full raw JSON - fine, though the JSON itself should be humanised.
Table clipped with no horizontal scroll - Receive button and STO id column unreachable for a real user.
Long 'SAP Delivery Notif: ...' string wraps one token per line in the narrow STO column, making rows very tall.

action_items: CRITICAL: make the Playwright chromium binary reachable from the supervisor backend process - add PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH to backend/.env (value /pw-browsers in this container) and restart backend, plus a deployment step running `python -m playwright install --with-deps chromium`. Without this every receive job fails with 'Executable doesn't exist'. My symlink workaround (/root/.cache/ms-playwright -> /pw-browsers) is test-env only and will not survive a rebuild.

HIGH: fix or remove the Received Qty override - SAP returns 'Changing data not possible; data is read-only' for the InboundDeliveryItemQuantityCollection PATCH (verified on a fresh delivery), yet the job still posts the FULL quantity and toasts 'received in full'. Set the quantity in the Playwright PGR screen, or fail the job with a clear message when an override cannot be applied.
HIGH: surface job.error in the failure toast (read the thrown Error's message, not just e.response.data.detail) and refresh the list / show an inline error when a job fails.
MEDIUM: add a catch-all route in App.js so unknown paths don't render a blank page (this is the whole 'blank page' report - the page itself is fine at /inventory/inbound-receipts).
MEDIUM: change the list wrapper to overflow-x-auto so the Receive button is reachable on tablet/mobile.
MEDIUM: add an in-progress guard so the same STO cannot have two concurrent receive jobs.
LOW: humanise SAP error strings, add a max on Received Qty, and reword the success toast when quantities were reduced.
critical_code_review_comments: inbound_receipt_service.apply_quantity_overrides swallows every exception per delivery as a WARNING - a failed override silently changes the business outcome (full instead of partial receipt). It must propagate or at least be returned to the caller and reflected in the job result.
server.py is 6125 lines - well past the 700-line guideline; the inbound-receipts routes belong in their own router module.

job_store.create_job/update_job/get_job are synchronous pymongo calls made directly from async handlers and from inside the background task; wrap in asyncio.to_thread like the neighbouring inbound_receipt_service calls.

The background job is a bare asyncio.create_task with no STO-level lock and no cancellation/timeout; a hot reload mid-run orphans it (job_store.recover_orphaned_jobs helps, but only at startup) and concurrent callers can double-post a real SAP Goods Receipt.
GET /inbound-receipts/pending performs unbounded SAP lookups (_backfill_missing_delivery_ids) inside the request path - move to a background backfill so the page load is not hostage to SAP latency.
Frontend pollReceiveJob is an unbounded while(true) with no max-attempts/deadline; if the job doc TTL-expires (24h) or a poll 404s, the user only gets the generic error toast.
updated_files: /root/.cache/ms-playwright (symlink to /pw-browsers - TEST ENV WORKAROUND, not app code)

success_rate.backend: 100% (13/13 pytest; 2/2 live end-to-end receive jobs succeeded after the Playwright env fix - 0% before it)
success_rate.frontend: 85% (page render, site filter, expand rows, dialog, validation, non-closable-while-submitting, progress polling, toast, refresh all pass; qty-override, failure-message and responsive layout fail)

rca_of_the_issue: 1) BLANK PAGE (reported): not a bug in InboundReceiptsPage. The route registered in App.js:119 is /inventory/inbound-receipts; the main agent loaded /inbound-receipts, which matches no <Route> and, because App.js has no catch-all, renders an empty <Routes> plus the shared Footer - hence 'only a footer visible'. Reproduced exactly (body text = 'Build c78a544 · 28 Aug 2026', page testid count = 0) and confirmed the correct URL renders the full page with 0 console errors. 2) ALL RECEIVE JOBS FAILING: playwright resolves its browser registry from PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH; that var is exported in interactive shells (=/pw-browsers, where chromium_headless_shell-1234 really exists) but is absent from the supervisor-launched uvicorn process, which therefore looked in /root/.cache/ms-playwright (non-existent) and raised 'Executable doesn't exist' ~20s after job start. Symlinking the default path to /pw-browsers made the identical flow succeed twice end-to-end, proving the code path itself is sound. 3) QUANTITY OVERRIDE: this SAP tenant returns HTTP 500 'Changing data not possible; data is read-only' for PATCH InboundDeliveryItemQuantityCollection('<id>') - i.e. the same tenant-level write restriction that disabled PGRBackground also blocks the quantity PATCH. apply_quantity_overrides catches the exception per delivery and only logs a warning, so the job proceeds and posts the full quantity while reporting success.
